title: Local Citation Building: Getting Your Business Listed on Every Directory - Tips

facts.fact: The vendor Adwave says its own data shows businesses with NAP consistency across 50+ quality directories often see a 25-35% lift in local pack visibility over time.
facts.quote: Our own data shows that businesses achieving **NAP** consistency across **50+** quality directories often see a **25-35%** lift in their local pack visibility over time.

facts.fact: Adwave states that local citations have become a top-5 local SEO ranking factor in 2026; this is the vendor's claim and no third-party source is cited.
facts.quote: Local citations have cemented their place as a top-5 local SEO ranking factor in 2026

facts.fact: The page defines local citations as mentions of a business's Name, Address, and Phone number (NAP) across the web.
facts.quote: They are simply mentions of your business's Name, Address, and Phone number (what we in the SEO world call **NAP**) across the web.

facts.fact: The page describes the local pack as the top three map results shown for searches such as 'dental clinic near me'.
facts.quote: those top three map results that show up for searches like

facts.fact: The page recommends four starting manual searches for a citation audit: business name, business name plus city, business phone number, and old business address if the business has moved.
facts.quote: I always recommend starting with these queries:

facts.fact: The page lists four report categories that a listing-management service such as Moz Local can produce: active, inconsistent, duplicate, and missing citations.
facts.quote: A listing-management service such as [Moz Local](https://moz.com/products/local) can report on:

facts.fact: The page states that a full citation audit is not optional and should be completed before building new business listings.
facts.quote: This first step (a full citation audit) isn't optional.

facts.fact: The page advises fixing listings in priority order, starting with Google, Apple Maps, and Facebook, then Yelp, then smaller niche directories.
facts.quote: Start with the big-name platforms like Google, Apple Maps, and Facebook.

facts.fact: The article was published on March 4, 2026.
